findings.description: Regular expression with nested quantifiers vulnerable to ReDoS: pattern uses `[^:]*` which can cause catastrophic backtracking
findings.reasoning: The pattern `^%%([^:]*):[ \t]*(.*)[ \t]*$` contains nested quantifiers with overlapping character classes. When a malicious input ends with many spaces instead of matching the expected format, the regex engine will backtrack extensively trying different splits of `[^:]*` and the following `[ \t]*`, leading to exponential time complexity. An attacker can send a long string with no colon and many trailing whitespace characters to trigger ReDoS.
